chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥamzah al-ʿAlawī, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, Muḥammad ibn Muslim, and Abū Baṣīr, who said: We said to him, “A well from which wudu (ablution) is performed, with urine flowing near it—does that render it najis?” They said: So he said:

If the well is at the upper part of the valley, and urine flows in the valley below it, and between them there is a distance of three cubits or four cubits, that does not render the well najis in any way. And if the well is at the lower part of the valley, and the water passes over it, and between the well and it there are seven cubits, it does not render it najis; but if it is less than that, wudu (ablution) is not to be performed from it.

Zurārah said: So I said to him, “What if it flows right alongside it and does not remain on the ground?” He said, “So long as it has no settled standing place, there is no harm in it. But if a little of it settles, then it does not pierce the earth, nor does it sink through it until it reaches the well, and there is no harm upon the well from it, so perform wudu (ablution) from it. That applies only when all the water has collected and become stagnant.”

key_terms.أَذْرُعٍ: cubits, used here as a legal measure of distance
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine, the source of najasah discussed here
key_terms.الْبِئْرُ: the well from which water is drawn
key_terms.الْوَادِي: the valley or channel through which liquid flows
key_terms.قَرَارٌ: a settled resting place where water remains

ai.seo_question: When does nearby flowing urine or drainage make well water unsuitable for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings about the purity of well water when urine or drainage flows near it. It distinguishes between the well’s position, the measured distance from contamination, and whether the water remains stagnant or merely passes by, in determining whether wudu (ablution) may be performed from it.
